userStories.title: Restructure Commands/: CommandBuilder + category subfolders
userStories.description: As a developer adding or navigating commands, I want Build() boilerplate consolidated and commands grouped by category so that I can find commands quickly and adding a new one requires no repeated wiring code.
acceptanceCriteria: A new CommandBuilder fluent API exists that wraps CommandOptionFactory and provides at minimum: .Argument<T>(), .Solution(), .DryRun(), .Handler()
Migrating MakeSealedCommand.Build() to CommandBuilder reduces its line count and eliminates its contribution to the top find-duplicates groups
After full rollout, rt analyze find-duplicates shows no Commands/Build() group with score > 4 or occurrences > 4
rt analyze list-smells LongMethod count for Commands/ is measurably lower than pre-migration baseline
The 49 Commands/ files are reorganised into Commands/Inspect/, Commands/Analyze/, Commands/Refactor/ subfolders using rt refactor move
Namespace remains RoslynTools.Commands throughout — no namespace split between folders
App.Discover() reflection-based registry continues to find all commands after the folder move
rt dump-help output is identical before and after (same commands, same groups, same help text)
All existing tests pass; no tests added purely to justify the refactor
userStories.notes: P2. Signal from rt analyze find-duplicates (groups scoring 4.4-7.2, 8-17 occurrences each, all in Commands/*.Build()). Two parts: (1) introduce CommandBuilder fluent wrapper over CommandOptionFactory, migrate MakeSealedCommand first, then dogfood with find-duplicates to confirm scores drop, then roll out; (2) move 49 flat files into Inspect/Analyze/Refactor subfolders using rt refactor move. Namespace stays RoslynTools.Commands. Plan at ~/.claude/plans/how-could-we-restructure-curried-harp.md.
